I've been wanting to do the same for quite a while and dicovered Campbell Island, literally in the middle of the sea between New Zealand and Antarctica, it is completely uninhabited and contains no research stations or anything.

It is however a UNESCO wildlife reserve and Important bird area and therefore landing a craft on it is forbidden, but I am quite sure that you could do it and it would take quite a while for NZ to realize because of its remoteness.

The climate and geography are quite hospitable but nowhere near unlivable as there is similar climates in Canada and Chile that people survive in. The temperatures range from 21c to -7c (70f to 17f) with quite high wind chill factor. There is only one tree on the island but it would be very easy to plant more for fuel/materials.

Food would be an issue because of said climate, the last time anyone stepped foot on the island they lasted ~2 weeks and then died of starvation because of the difficulty growing food, this could probably be solved with the construction of greenhouses that would allow less hardy foods to be grown. Protein would have to come from fish or vegetables as there is no way of sustaining cattle or pigs in the temperatures.
